company: CRACKER BARREL OLD COUNTRY STORE, INC.

rfm_tuples.R: FY25 10-K (filed 2025-09-26) implies management conviction in the multi-year 'strategic transformation plan' and brand refresh; CEO Masino's letter and Item 7 frame the strategy as additive: 'we plan to continue to leverage and build on that strength.'
rfm_tuples.f: Parse EDGAR ownership.xml for every Form 4 filed between 2025-05-25 and 2026-05-25; classify by transaction code (P = open-market purchase, S = sale, F = tax-withholding on RSU vest, A = grant, M = option exercise). Mode B: given the stock is down 54% from peak, would expect at least some C-suite/director buying if management believed turnaround thesis.
rfm_tuples.M_source: form4 (m_sources.form4 — EDGAR ownership.xml direct parse, 448 Form 4 filings, 740 non-derivative transactions parsed)
rfm_tuples.M_value: ZERO open-market PURCHASES (code P) by any named officer or director of CBRL in the 12 months pre-cutoff. The only code-P transactions in the entire dataset were by external 10%+ holders (GMT Capital Corp Apr-May 2025 at $35-44, BEFORE the logo fiasco, who then turned around and sold heavily into the Dec 2025 weakness at $25-29 — see CBRL-02). CEO Julie Masino's only 12mo transactions: 6,566 sh tax-withhold (F) on 2025-09-30 @ $44.06 and 688 sh (F) on 2025-08-07 @ $57.58, plus two grant receipts (A) on 2025-09-25. CFO Craig Pommells: option exercise (M) 1,073 sh and tax-withhold (F) 6,851 sh, all on 2025-09-30. Across ALL 27 named executives, 12mo activity decomposes to 19 F (forced tax-withholdings), 15 A (grants), 7 M (option exercises), 0 S, 0 P. Stock declined from ~$57 (Aug 2025) to ~$22 (May 2026) — a textbook insider-conviction window — and not a single officer or director chose to add personal capital.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: This is the cleanest negative Form-4 signal Signal OS can produce. Management is talking about a turnaround, the activist (Biglari) is publicly demanding accountability, the stock is off 54%, and yet zero insiders are willing to put $1 of personal cash at risk. Per the framework spec ('absence of expected buying' = escalate to SEVERE), this is the canonical SHORT-confirming tape. Contrast with ABG (CEO bought $1M into drawdown) or other LONG-tier names in this cohort where insiders ADD.

rfm_tuples.R: Implied: external smart-money holders (e.g., GMT Capital, the only 10%+ public buyer Apr-May 2025) maintain their thesis through the proxy fight and FY26 disclosures.
rfm_tuples.f: Cross-reference GMT Capital's Form 4 buy cluster (Apr-May 2025) with subsequent Form 4 sell cluster, then cross-check against the public 13G/A filings to identify what GMT learned between Apr 2025 and Dec 2025.
rfm_tuples.M_value: GMT Capital bought 487,400 sh open-market across Apr 4 - May 7, 2025 for ~$20.1M at avg $41.30 (peaked $44.60 on May 7). They then REVERSED: 14 sell transactions Dec 2-31 2025 + Jan 5 2026 totaling 593,200 sh for ~$15.3M at avg $25.78 — i.e., realizing roughly a 38% loss and a $4.8M absolute haircut on their cost basis in roughly 7 months. The Dec 2025 sells began three days BEFORE Q1 FY26 earnings (filed Dec 9, 2025 — first net loss of -$24.6M) — suggesting smart-money knew Q1 would be bad. Confirming SC 13G/A: GMT's beneficial ownership fell from 2,240,200 sh (2026-02-13 filing) to 1,590,700 sh (2026-05-15 filing) — another 649,500 sh sold in Q1-Q2 calendar 2026, on top of the Dec 2025 sells. Separately, FMR LLC (Fidelity passive) dropped from 1,212,289 sh to 700,261 sh between Feb 5 and May 6, 2026 (-42%, -512,028 sh).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B catch: the one identifiable smart-money buyer covering the public Form-4 tape spent 7 months unwinding their position at a substantial loss, and timed exit windows around bad news disclosures. The proxy-fight inflows ($20M peak position) became proxy-fight outflows BEFORE the proxy vote and through Q2 earnings. This contradicts any narrative that 'institutional smart money is accumulating'.

rfm_tuples.R: 'In 2024, as part of our multi-year strategic plan, we made the decision to reduce our quarterly dividends.' (FY25 10-K)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — verify the dividend cut magnitude and trajectory. Mode B — given the issuer frames this as a strategic choice to reinvest, is the resulting cash position consistent with that framing or is it actually distress?
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (10-K statement of equity FY23/FY24/FY25 + Q1/Q2 FY26 10-Qs)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Dividend per share trajectory: FY23 $5.20 (paid $115.9M); FY24 $4.15 (paid $93.3M, -20%); FY25 $1.00 (paid $22.8M, -76%); FY26 H1 $0.25/quarter run-rate ($0.50 paid YTD, $11.2M). This is a >80% cut from peak. CBRL has paid quarterly dividends for ~four decades; the cut accelerated from -20% (FY24) to -76% (FY25). The 'reinvest in strategy' framing is undermined by the OUTCOME: cash position fell from $39.6M (8/1/2025) to $8.6M (1/30/2026), revolver borrowings rose from $0 to $45.5M, and operating cash flow turned NEGATIVE in H1 FY26. Mode B: the dividend cut wasn't optional reallocation, it was forced by the cash burn during transformation.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The framing 'we chose to reinvest' is technically true but functionally misleading: the cash freed by the dividend cut was consumed by operating losses and proxy expenses, not by accretive growth investment. Comparable restaurant traffic deteriorated FURTHER (-3.0% FY25 → -7.3% Q1 FY26 → -10.1% Q2 FY26).

rfm_tuples.R: Note 4 of FY25 10-K + Q2 FY26 10-Q: '$150,000 aggregate principal amount of the 2026 Notes matures on June 15, 2026, unless earlier converted, repurchased or redeemed.' Issuer asserts compliance with 2025 Revolving Credit Facility covenants.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — check cash runway against the June 15, 2026 cash maturity (21 days AFTER the 2026-05-25 cutoff) and stress-test refinancing.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (Q2 FY26 10-Q balance sheet, Note 4 debt schedule)
rfm_tuples.M_value: $150M of 0.625% convertible senior notes mature 2026-06-15 (21 days post-cutoff). At 1/30/2026, current portion of LTD = $149.6M (i.e., the entire 2026 Notes balance is current), cash = $8.6M, revolver drawn = $45.5M out of $550M (so $504.5M nominal capacity remains, less letters of credit). Q2 FY26 fair value of the 2026 Notes was $146.8M (i.e., trading slightly below par — convert is out of the money: conversion price $188.14/sh vs CBRL trading ~$22 = no upside conversion). Settlement will be ~$150M CASH out of the revolver. Post-settlement, revolver utilization rises to ~$195M (~36% of $550M). The 2030 Notes' fair value collapsed from $374M to $277M (-26%) in 6 months, signaling that the debt market re-priced CBRL credit. There is no liquidity crisis at cutoff (revolver has room), but cash flexibility is materially constrained and any further operating deterioration would compress the cushion.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B catch: the issuer's covenant-compliance statement is true but the disclosure does not foreground that the 2026 Notes have effectively zero conversion optionality at current prices and must be settled in cash by drawing the revolver, structurally moving leverage up. Combined with FY26 H1 operating-cash burn, this is a real (not catastrophic) balance-sheet headwind that frames why insiders won't buy.

rfm_tuples.R: 'In the first quarter of 2026, we introduced an updated logo, which received unfavorable consumer feedback and generated negative publicity. Other initiatives contemplated under our multi-year strategic plan may elicit similar adverse reactions.' (FY25 10-K Item 1A)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — verify the issuer's self-disclosure against subsequent quarter comp-sales evidence. Mode B — link the logo event to actual traffic impact and proxy-fight escalation.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (Q1 + Q2 FY26 10-Qs comp tables) + DEFC14A (Biglari proxy materials)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1 FY26 comp restaurant guest traffic -7.3% (vs -2.9% PY); Q2 FY26 comp traffic -10.1% (vs -2.7% PY); H1 average check rose only +3.1% — insufficient to offset traffic. Operating income (loss): Q1 -$32.8M (vs +$7.1M), Q2 +$0.5M (vs +$29.1M), H1 -$32.3M (vs +$36.2M, a $68.5M YoY operating-income SWING). Biglari DEFC14A (filed 2025-10-07): 'On August 19, 2025, the Company unveiled its new logo. The Company's market capitalization plunged over $160 million in the ensuing six days.' Trump's Truth Social post Aug 26 triggered the company to scrap the logo. The 10-K admits the issue but does NOT disclose Trump intervention or specific market-cap impact.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The issuer's disclosure is honest in description but incomplete in causal/political dimension. The traffic collapse is real and the magnitude (-10.1% Q2) is severe for a full-service restaurant — this is the operating-evidence side of the SHORT thesis. Honesty-alpha caveat: Signal OS gives no alpha credit for re-discovering this; the disclosure itself does the work. The signal here is the INTERACTION with no-insider-buying (CBRL-01) and dividend cut (CBRL-03).

rfm_tuples.R: Annual meeting (11/20/2025): all ten management nominees presented as the company's slate. Item 5.07 8-K (11/24/2025).
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — verify the actual vote outcome by director.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Vote outcome (Item 5.07): Director Gilbert Dávila received 6,716,130 FOR vs 9,570,461 AGAINST (i.e., FAILED to receive majority support) and resigned effective same day; board reduced from 10 to 9. CEO Julie Masino received 12,130,721 FOR vs 4,116,283 AGAINST (25.4% against — abnormally high for an incumbent CEO). Other directors: Jody Bilney 32.6% against; Cheryl Henry 9.0% against. The Biglari-led dissident campaign (DEFC14A filed 10/7/2025, with 6+ DFAN14As Oct-Nov 2025) succeeded in ousting one Compensation Committee Chair and registered a substantial protest vote against the CEO. Proxy-contest costs in FY26 H1: $4.1M ($2.6M in Q2 alone).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The board claimed unity but lost a director (Dávila, the marketing committee chair Biglari specifically targeted as responsible for the logo fiasco) — a rare event signaling genuine shareholder displeasure beyond the activist's own bloc. The 25% against-vote on the CEO is a yellow flag — most S&P 600 CEOs see <5% against. Independent verification: the public DEFC14A's central claim ('$160M market-cap destruction in 6 days post-logo') was concretely supported by the Q1 FY26 operating loss and the Dec 2025 GMT exit.

rfm_tuples.R: FY25 10-K: $19.8M impairment in FY25 (7 Cracker Barrel + 25 MSBC stores) vs $17.4M FY24. Q1 FY26: zero impairment; Q2 FY26: $0.4M impairment (3 MSBC lease non-renewals).
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — given the operating collapse in H1 FY26 (-$32M operating loss), absence of impairment in Q1 is suspicious; check for store-closure trigger and goodwill testing.
rfm_tuples.M_value: MSBC store count: 69 (8/2024) → 68 (8/2025) → 54 (10/2025) → 54 (1/2026). The 14 MSBC closures in Q1 FY26 generated only $3.5M of closing costs (lease termination), notably WITHOUT a corresponding impairment hit, because the chain had already impaired the underlying long-lived assets in FY25 ($18.4M). However, Cracker Barrel parent brand goodwill ($2M residual after FY24 goodwill impairment) and 657 Cracker Barrel locations' carrying value have NOT been re-tested at the FY26 H1 traffic run-rate. With Q2 traffic -10.1% and operating margins inverting, expect FY26 annual impairment to materially exceed FY25's $19.8M. Issuer discloses risk in 10-K Item 1A ('Long-lived assets ... may not be recoverable') but does not provide a sensitivity table for restaurant-level carrying values vs current traffic trends.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Disclosure is technically compliant (FY25 impairment was booked and quantified) but the absence of any Q1/Q2 FY26 store-level impairment in a quarter when operating cash flow turned negative is a Mode-B gap. Auditor (Deloitte, ratified 11/20/2025) issued clean FY25 opinion. Expect a Q3 or Q4 FY26 impairment catch-up — typical pattern for chronic underperformance is annual rather than quarterly testing.

rfm_tuples.R: 'We were in compliance with the 2025 Revolving Credit Facility's financial covenants at January 30, 2026, and we expect to be in compliance ... for the remaining term of the facility.' (Q2 FY26 10-Q)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — quantify covenant headroom given the H1 operating loss and check the dividend-eligibility leverage trigger (3.50x consolidated total leverage ratio).
rfm_tuples.M_value: Quantitative covenants: max consolidated total leverage ratio and min consolidated interest coverage ratio. The 10-K specifies a 3.50x leverage trigger for unlimited dividend payments; above that, dividends capped at $100M/yr. Estimated FY25 leverage (long-term debt $335.5M + 2026 Notes $149.2M + leases ~$650M operating + $30M finance ≈ $1.16B / FY25 EBITDA ~$170M-180M proxy from operating income $55M + D&A $122M) ≈ 6.5x lease-adjusted, ~2.7x without leases. Without lease capitalization, CBRL is below the 3.50x trigger. H1 FY26 operating loss compresses TTM EBITDA, and the dividend was already cut to $0.25/q ($22M/yr) which is well below the $100M cap, suggesting the company is operating in the >3.50x band where dividend payments are restricted to $100M and have already been right-sized. No reported covenant breach, no waiver, no going-concern flag in Q2.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Statement is factually correct but the math implies meaningful covenant headroom compression. Not severe — no breach, no going concern — but the leverage ratio trajectory is the wrong direction for a turnaround story. Combined with the $150M 2026 convert maturity in June (CBRL-04), this is a balance sheet under stress, not in crisis.

rfm_tuples.R: Item 5.02 8-K (2026-05-01): General Counsel Richard Wolfson took early retirement May 1, 2026.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — pattern-check executive departures during distress periods.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Wolfson notified of intent to retire on 2025-12-05 (one day before Q1 FY26 10-Q was filed showing first net loss in years and within the same week the activist proxy contest concluded). Original retirement date 5/5/2026; Board accelerated to 5/1/2026 with a Consulting Agreement that terminated on same date. Replaced by VP/Deputy GC Jennifer Lankford (internal promotion). Looking at the broader picture: prior CEO Sandra Cochran (transactions through 2024) replaced by Julie Masino in 2023; Director Davila resigned 11/20/2025 after failing the majority vote. There has been turnover but no en-masse exodus.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Single GC retirement with internal succession is not a distress flag in isolation. The timing (announced day before Q1 net loss) deserves note but the Consulting Agreement framework suggests pre-planned succession rather than crisis exit. Neutral signal.

summary: CBRL is a -54% drawdown name where the Signal-OS forensic tape strongly CONFIRMS the SHORT thesis. The headline Form-4 signal is the absence of expected buying: across 448 Form 4 filings and 740 non-derivative transactions in the 12mo pre-cutoff window, ZERO officers or directors executed an open-market PURCHASE (code P). All 41 officer-12mo transactions decompose to forced tax-withholding (F), grants (A), and option exercises (M). The only smart-money buyer covering the public tape — GMT Capital — bought $20M Apr-May 2025 at ~$41 then reversed and sold $15M Dec 2025-Jan 2026 at ~$26 (estimated $4.8M realized loss) AND continued unwinding into Q1-Q2 2026 (sold another 649,500 sh per 13G/A); FMR LLC dropped 42% of its position over the same window. The fundamental backdrop: dividend cut 80% from peak ($5.20 → $1.00), H1 FY26 operating loss -$32M (vs +$36M prior year), Q2 traffic -10.1%, cash $8.6M, revolver drawn $45M, $150M 2026 convertible matures 21 days post-cutoff requiring cash settlement that drives revolver utilization to ~36%. The proxy-fight outcome (director Davila received majority AGAINST votes and resigned; 25% against vote on CEO) signals genuine governance pressure. Disclosure quality is honest — logo fiasco, dividend cut, traffic collapse all clearly stated in 10-K and 10-Qs — so there is no fraud component. The alpha here is honesty-alpha exclusion: management is transparent, but the operating data + insider tape together say management does NOT believe in its own turnaround. Severity: 1 PASS / 1 UNVERIFIABLE / 4 MODERATE / 2 SEVERE / 1 RED_FLAG. Verdict: SHORT-tier.
